Route 3: Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD)

1. Place a piece of high-purity copper metal (Cu) as the source material inside a vacuum chamber of a PVD system.
2. Evacuate the chamber to a high vacuum (e.g., 10⁻⁶ Torr).
3. Heat the copper source using an electron beam or resistive heating until it begins to evaporate.
4. Deposit the evaporated copper atoms onto a silicon substrate placed a few centimeters above the source.Control the deposition rate to be approximately 0.1 nm/s.
5. Maintain the substrate temperature at 200 °C during deposition to improve film crystallinity.
6. Deposit a copper film with a thickness of 100 nm.
7. Turn off the heater and allow the substrate to cool to room temperature under vacuum. Remove the substrate to obtain the resultant copper film.

Final product: Сu as a thin film with a cubic crystal structure, film size ~10000x10000x0.1 nm, matching PDF reference 04-0836.
